get.description:
The rows a delete stamped rather than removed, kept up to date.

A shape is a filtered view of one table that a client subscribes to. This route is a proxy in front of the sync service: which rows exist in the shape — the tenant, the lifecycle predicate, and the application's own scoping — is decided by the server and cannot be influenced from here. Where the client is in the stream is forwarded untouched.

With `live=true` the request is a long poll: it does not answer until something changes, so a client timeout set for an ordinary request will cut it short.

The response body is the sync protocol's own and is not described here. The `electric-*` response headers carry the cursor: send `handle` and `offset` back on the next request, or the subscription starts over.

Requires a session scoped to a tenant, and the shape is filtered to it.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Where in the stream to resume, from the previous response's electric-offset.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The shape handle from a previous response. Omit it to start a new subscription.

parameters.name: live
parameters.description: Long-poll until something changes, rather than answering with what is there now.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The sync service's own cache-busting cursor, echoed back from the last response.

parameters.name: replica
parameters.description: Whether updates carry the whole row or only the columns that changed.

parameters.name: matchday
parameters.description: Restrict the shape to one matchday.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only lessons in this state.

200.description: A chunk of the shape, in the sync protocol's own format.

electric-handle.description: The shape handle. Send it back to continue this subscription.

electric-offset.description: Where this chunk ended. Send it back to resume from here.

electric-cursor.description: The cursor to echo on the next request.

electric-up-to-date.description: Present when the client has caught up with the shape.

X-Rig-Sync-Fallback.description: Present when this response is a snapshot served because the sync service could not be reached, rather than a chunk of a live subscription. The rows are correct as of the moment they were read and are not updated until the subscription resumes.

502.description: The sync service could not be reached, and this shape had nothing to answer with instead: no database was configured, this shape asked not to be answered from one, or the read failed or was larger than a snapshot may be.

503.description: The sync service could not be reached, and this subscription already holds a snapshot. Keep it and retry after Retry-After.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before polling again.

get.description:
A deletion stamps the row rather than removing it, so this is what was deleted and can still be brought back. Only rows inside the 30-day restore window appear: past it a row is gone as far as anyone is concerned, so it is not in the trash either.

Requires the `lesson.read` permission.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip before the first returned row.

post.description:
Search Lessons with filters.

The primary form of this operation is `QUERY /api/v1/lessons` — a read that carries a body, and so safe and idempotent in a way POST is not. OpenAPI 3.1 cannot describe an operation on the QUERY method, so it is documented here as the POST alias that exists for intermediaries which reject unfamiliar methods. One handler serves both routes and they answer identically.

Requires the `lesson.read` permission.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip before the first returned row.

409.description: The lesson was not in the Planned state.

post.description:
The deletion stamp is cleared and the row appears in reads again. It works for 30 days after the deletion; past that the row is no longer eligible and this answers 409.

Restoring a row that was never deleted is not an error. It is already in the state the caller asked for, and answering otherwise would make a retry of a request whose response went missing look like a failure.

The request carries no fields. What to do when the world has moved on while the row was retired — a unique value taken by something created since — is the application's decision, and it is made in the restore hook: refuse, or change the row so that it fits.

Every rule then runs against whatever the hook settled on, not only the ones for fields it touched. The row was not live, so nothing about it has been checked against the world it is returning to.

Requires the `lesson.write` permission.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the Lesson.

post.summary: Put a Lesson back to one of its previous versions.
post.description:
The version is replayed through the ordinary update path rather than written over the row, so the state being replaced is itself snapshotted first and every rule an update runs still runs. Reverting is undoable, and a value that would be refused now is still refused.

Requires the `lesson.write` permission.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the Lesson.

200.description: The Lesson, as of the version replayed.

get.description:
Every update copies the row as it was before writing the change, so this is the row's history: newest first, and never the live row itself.

These do not appear in ordinary reads. A version answers Get by its own identifier, but it is filtered out of List and Search, so history does not turn up in a listing.

Requires the `lesson.read` permission.

parameters.description: Identifier of the Lesson.

200.description: The versions of the Lesson, newest first.

BadRequest.description:
The request was malformed or a parameter could not be parsed.

The body's `code` is `BadRequest`.

Unauthorized.description:
No valid session or API key was presented.

The body's `code` is `Unauthorized`.

Forbidden.description:
The caller is known but not permitted to do this.

The body's `code` is `Forbidden`.

NotFound.description:
No such resource, or it belongs to another tenant.

The body's `code` is `NotFound`.

Conflict.description:
The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.

The body's `code` is `Conflict`.

UnprocessableEntity.description:
The request was well-formed but failed validation.

The body's `code` is `UnprocessableEntity`.

RateLimited.description:
Too many requests. Retry after the interval in the Retry-After header.

The body's `code` is `RateLimited`.

Internal.description:
Something went wrong on the server.

The body's `code` is `Internal`.

ApiRevision.name: API-Revision
ApiRevision.description: The API revision this client was built against. A server generated from an older document than the caller expects answers 426 rather than guessing.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A key of the caller's choosing, so a retried write happens once. Sending the same key with the same body replays the first answer and sets Idempotency-Replayed; with a different body it is refused with 422, and while the first is still in flight, with 409.

IdempotencyReplayed.description: Present and true when this answer is a replay of an earlier request carrying the same Idempotency-Key, rather than work done again.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests permitted in the current window.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the current window resets.
